site.name: harborwallet-mobile
site.summary: harborwallet-mobile Fictional consumer wallet "Harbor Wallet" iOS-style phone fixture. Single-page app simulating a 390 × 844 device frame with notch, status bar, home indicator, and tab bar. UXBench fixture in the Mobile Micro-UI category. Layout - **Phone chassis** — 12 px chrome + radial gradient backdrop. Renders edge-to-edge on actual mobile (≤460 px viewport). - **Status bar** — live ticking time (rounded down to minutes), signal bars, wifi, battery (78%). - **Tab bar** (bottom) — 5 tabs: Home / Send / Receive / Activity / Account. Screens | `data-screen` | Highlights |

explored_user_goal: Autonomously explore and critique the UX of the full harborwallet-mobile system, prioritizing the primary settings/privacy flow plus adjacent pages, states, and recovery paths.
exploration_summary: Harbor Wallet's mobile prototype exhibits significant interaction gaps and widespread mobile accessibility issues. Critical actions like Sign out, QR scanning, and Swap produce no feedback, and the Receive screen's segmented control is entirely non-functional. Furthermore, a systemic pattern of undersized tap targets across headers, segmented controls, and action buttons severely hampers touch usability, creating friction for core financial tasks.

exploration_plan.goal: Exhaustively explore and critique the UX of the Harbor Wallet mobile fixture, focusing on the primary settings/privacy flow and adjacent screens, while validating all interactive states and mobile viewport constraints.
exploration_plan.summary: The exploration will navigate through the app's primary tab-based screens (Home, Send, Receive, Activity, Account) to validate core wallet flows. It will then dive deep into the Account screen to uncover and test the settings/privacy features. Finally, it will re-run critical checks on a mobile viewport to validate layout warnings and responsive behavior within the simulated device frame.
assumptions: The Account tab (◉ Account) contains or leads to the settings/privacy features mentioned in the user goal.
The app is a single-page application where tab buttons and action buttons toggle visibility of different data-screens rather than navigating to new HTML files.
The '3 🔔' button will trigger a notification panel or modal, which may contain privacy-related alerts.
The layout warnings for small tap targets (38x38px and 42x16px) will be more pronounced and impactful during the mobile viewport testing phase.
risk_hotspots: Small tap targets: '3 🔔' (38x38px) and 'See all' (42x16px) failing mobile accessibility guidelines.
Settings/Privacy controls: Potential for unclear toggles, missing confirmation dialogs for destructive privacy actions, or obscured navigation paths.
Send/Receive flows: Risk of missing input validation, unclear error states, or dead-end modals in the simulated UI.
Viewport overflow: Content within the simulated phone chassis might overflow or clip incorrectly on actual mobile viewports (≤460px).

phases.title: Home & Quick Actions
phases.objective: Validate the Home screen layout, asset display, and quick action button behaviors.
key_checks: Verify '3 🔔' button interaction and any notification panel appearance.
Click 'See all' for Recent Activity and verify navigation/transitions.
Test quick action buttons: ↑ Send, ↓ Receive, ⇄ Swap, + Top up.
Check for dynamic updates in the status bar (time ticking).
exit_criteria: Quick actions verified to trigger screen transitions or modals.

phases.title: Core Transaction Screens
phases.objective: Explore the Send, Receive, and Activity screens for usability, form validation, and state changes.
key_checks: Navigate to Send screen, test input field, and verify available controls.
Navigate to Receive screen, check for address/QR code display and copy/share actions.
Navigate to Activity screen, verify transaction list and filtering/interaction capabilities.
Attempt invalid input in the Send form to check error handling.
exit_criteria: Send, Receive, and Activity screens fully inspected.
Input interactions and validation states tested.
All visible buttons on these screens clicked.

phases.title: Account & Privacy Deep Dive
phases.objective: Locate and thoroughly test the Settings and Privacy controls under the Account tab.
key_checks: Navigate to Account screen and identify entry points to Settings/Privacy.
Toggle privacy settings (e.g., data sharing, analytics) and verify state retention if possible.
Check for clear labels, descriptions, and confirmations on privacy-impacting actions.
Explore other Account sub-sections (e.g., profile, security, help).
exit_criteria: Settings/Privacy screens located and fully interacted with.
All toggles/inputs in privacy settings exercised.
Navigation back to main Account screen verified.

phases.title: Mobile Viewport Validation
phases.objective: Re-test critical flows and layout warnings on a mobile viewport to ensure responsive compliance.
key_checks: Switch to mobile viewport and verify the phone chassis renders edge-to-edge (≤460px).
Re-validate tapping the small '3 🔔' and 'See all' targets for usability.
Check Account/Settings/Privacy flow for layout overflow or clipping issues on small screens.
Verify tab bar accessibility and hit areas on mobile.
exit_criteria: Mobile viewport renders correctly without horizontal scroll.
Small tap targets explicitly tested and critiqued.
Primary settings/privacy flow completed successfully on mobile.

coverage_targets.pages: Cover all virtual screens (data-screens) within index.html triggered by the tab bar and actions.
coverage_targets.features: Interact with all 39 buttons, 1 link, and 1 input detected in the prescan, focusing on privacy toggles and transaction inputs.
coverage_targets.mobile: Validate all layout warnings and complete the primary settings/privacy flow on a mobile viewport.

notes: Since this is a single-page app with a simulated phone frame, pay close attention to whether interactions correctly update the DOM/data-screen attributes or if they are just visual placeholders.
Keep an eye out for any console or network errors triggered by button clicks, as the prescan showed none initially.

findings.user_goal: Sign out of the account securely
findings.problem: Clicking the 'Sign out' button performs no visible action and provides no confirmation dialog, leaving the user logged in and unsure if the action registered.
findings.evidence: Clicking the 'Sign out' button (ux-41) resulted in no visible state change, dialog, or navigation, failing to provide a confirmation step for a destructive action. (steps-13-18)
findings.why_it_matters: Destructive actions like signing out require confirmation to prevent accidental logouts and potential loss of unsaved state, which is especially critical in a financial app.
findings.suggestion: Implement a confirmation modal or sheet when 'Sign out' is tapped, asking the user to verify their intent before ending the session.

findings.user_goal: Receive money via bank or crypto
findings.problem: The segmented control for receive methods (In-app, Bank, Crypto) is non-functional; tapping 'Bank' or 'Crypto' does not update the displayed content, trapping the user on the 'In-app' view.
findings.evidence: Clicking the 'Bank' and 'Crypto' tabs (ux-35, ux-36) resulted in no visible text or URL change, confirming the entire segmented control is non-functional. (steps-07-12)
findings.why_it_matters: Users expecting to see bank details or a crypto wallet address for receiving funds are left stranded, making the feature broken for those specific flows.
findings.suggestion: Ensure the segmented control updates the view with the appropriate receiving instructions and details for each tab, or disable unimplemented tabs with a visual indicator.

findings.user_goal: Send money via QR code or swap assets
findings.problem: Tapping the 'QR' and '⇄ Swap' buttons results in dead taps with no visual feedback, modals, or navigation, leaving users uncertain if the app is unresponsive.
findings.evidence: Clicking the 'QR' button (ux-13) and '⇄ Swap' button produced no visible change, URL change, or modal, indicating they are non-functional stubs lacking interaction feedback. (steps-31-36)
findings.why_it_matters: Dead taps erode user trust, especially in a wallet app where users expect responsive and reliable interactions for financial operations.
findings.suggestion: Either implement the QR scanner and Swap flows, or provide clear disabled states/toasts indicating these features are coming soon.

findings.problem: The '📨 Send link' and '📷 Save image' buttons on the Receive screen provide no feedback upon tapping, failing to confirm whether the link was sent or the image was saved.
findings.evidence: Clicking '📨 Send link' (ux-40) and '📷 Save image' (ux-41) produced no visible text change, toast, or modal, failing to provide interaction feedback. (steps-49-53)
findings.why_it_matters: Without confirmation, users may repeatedly tap the button or assume the app is broken, leading to duplicate actions or abandonment of the flow.
findings.suggestion: Display a brief toast notification (e.g., 'Link copied to clipboard' or 'Image saved to photos') to confirm the action was successful.

findings.problem: Tapping the notification bell icon with an active badge (3) produces no visible change, panel, or feedback, creating a dead-end interaction.
findings.evidence: Clicking the notification bell (ux-1) produced no visible change or feedback, indicating a missing interaction state or dead-end for an active notification badge. (steps-01-06)
findings.why_it_matters: An active notification badge promises information; ignoring taps on it frustrates users and hides potentially important account alerts.
findings.suggestion: Open a notification panel or dropdown list when the bell is tapped, or remove the badge if the feature is not yet implemented.

findings.user_goal: Navigate the app and trigger actions comfortably
findings.problem: There is a systemic pattern of undersized tap targets across the app, with headers (36x36px), segmented controls (32px height), quick-fill buttons (25px height), and action buttons (41px height) all falling below the 44px mobile guidance.
findings.evidence: Layout warnings consistently flagged small tap targets: back/share buttons (36x36px, 37x30px), segmented tabs (101x32px), quick-amount chips (25px height), and Receive action buttons (41px height). (steps-01-06, steps-43-48, steps-49-53)
findings.why_it_matters: Undersized touch targets cause mis-taps and interaction friction, making the app difficult to use for people with motor impairments or larger fingers.
findings.suggestion: Increase the padding and height of all interactive elements to meet the minimum 44x44px touch target guideline, particularly for frequently used controls like headers and segmented tabs.

findings.problem: Tapping the settings gear icon (⚙) on the Account screen does not navigate to a settings view, blocking access to the Legal & privacy section.
findings.evidence: Clicking the ⚙️ settings icon (ux-12) did not navigate to a settings screen; the app remained on the Account screen with no visible change. (steps-37-42)
findings.why_it_matters: Users cannot access critical privacy controls or legal information if the entry point is unresponsive, reducing transparency and trust.
findings.suggestion: Wire the gear icon to navigate to the Legal & privacy screen, or make the 'Legal & privacy' list item directly tappable.

gaps: 38% of actions produced no visible URL/text change; this may indicate dead controls or repeated probes.
